articleTitle: Investigation of Strength of E91 Quantum Key Distribution Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This article is about studying how strong the E91 quantum key distribution protocol is. The protocol uses the ideas of quantum mechanics. Quantum cryptography is a very hopeful field in keeping information safe, and the E91 protocol is seen as one of the most hopeful ways to guarantee complete and certain secure transmission of data. The aim of the study is to find weaknesses in the E91 protocol and understand how well it can withstand different kinds of quantum attacks. This work uses math and computer simulations to carefully study and make sure the protocol is secure. The literature review discusses previous studies on quantum cryptography and protocols for distributing keys. This study will help make better E91 protocols and will be important for keeping information safe in modern communication systems. These discoveries can help make quantum cryptography better and more useful in real-life situations. It can secure data by protecting it from increasing cyber-attacks and make sure that information systems work well.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Information Processing with Relative Priority and Different Service Intensity
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a model of information processing with priorities. The peculiarity of the model is that the system receives two flows of different types of data of different intensity. Thus we may operate with two classes of customers. The first class of the customers are priority. In this paper, we consider a system with a relative priority. It means that the arrived priority customer does not push out a customer of the second class, if the last one is servicing by a server. The service time of customers is random with an exponential probability distribution. Each type of customer has its own service duration. It is supposed that each class of customers has its own queue. The queue sizes are the same. Limiting the length of queues is the reason for the system to work with losses. It means that if at the time of receipt of a customer the server is idle, then a customer immediately gets up for service; if the server is busy servicing another customer, and there is a place in the queue, the newly received customer enters the waiting queue, otherwise it is lost. We suggest a system of equations for stationary probabilities and an original numerical implementation of finding the system's probability distribution. We also obtain the characteristics of the QoS parameters of customers - the probability of receiving a customer for instant service, the probability of getting into the system regardless of priority, the loss probability for priority customers, the loss probability for non-priority customers, the probability of refusing to service a customer of any class, the probability that the server is currently serves the customer of the first class, the probability that the server is currently servicing the customer of the second class.

Author Keywords: Mathematical model of information processing with relative priority

articleTitle: Determining Web Application Vulnerabilities Using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Information technology is a significant factor in the modern world. This area is developing quickly, becoming essential as new, more complex protection methods appear. Threat detection instruments have also been actively developing for recent decades. The available scanning systems allow to disclose many threats. Moreover, machine and deep learning Artificial intelligence methods have been developing significantly. With so many penetration testing scanners available, choosing the most effective scanner can be daunting as it depends on the specific testing environment. This paper focuses on detecting SQL injection threats with the use of such machine learning algorithms as Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost. The analyzed dataset contains safe and dangerous SQL commands that various websites have been exposed to. The classification model results showed that most applied algorithms demonstrated perfect accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score values above 0.95. These high scores proved to be efficient in the SQL injection classification tasks.

articleTitle: Simulation of Air Pollution Monitoring using Geosensors Placed on Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Urban air pollution is one of the environmental issues in most countries. The presence of harmful substances in the air leads to many human health problems. Therefore, monitoring air pollution is an important task that have been solved jointly by scientists, environmentalists, and government services. The relevance of environmental monitoring lies in the fact that it can be used to identify the main problems associated with environmental imbalance. To know the current state of air pollution in the city, it is necessary not only to monitor the concentration of pollutants in the air, but also to model possible options for the emission of harmful substances and their distribution in the environment. It is necessary to use mathematical models of the dispersion of pollution zones, taking into account various parameters, such as wind direction and speed, air temperature, time of day, etc. Currently, to improve the quality of monitoring, systems are used where geosensors are placed on moving objects. Data about the presence of harmful substances in the atmosphere collected by sensors are transmitted wirelessly to the center for processing to compile a geofield of the controlled area. The authors present a simulation model for a monitoring system whose sensors are placed on vehicles. Modeling results help optimize the data collection process and effectively manage air pollution monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Refinement of the Emission Source Identification Results
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: A hybrid emission source identification algorithm combining sensitivity operator-based and deep learning approaches is presented. A distributed emission sources estimate disregarding the point-wise structure of the “true” emission source is first obtained with general sensitivity operator-based algorithm. The algorithm produces both the source estimate and the sensitivity operator of the inverse problem. With the sensitivity operator, the aggregate is constructed that can be used to predict the result of the source identification in the considered conditions given the “true” source function. This aggregate can be applied to train the neural network to refine the source identification results by incorporating the a priori information of the unknown sources belonging to a specific class of multiple point-wise sources. The algorithm was tested in a remote-sensing inverse modeling scenario for the Baikal region. In the numerical experiments the convolution-type neural network was able to refine the inverse modeling results by providing the solution in the form of the localized point- wise sources.

articleTitle: Method for Solving Multidimensional Problems of Optimizing the Parameters of High-power Klystrons
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive random search algorithm is proposed for solving nonlinear multidimensional problems with local constrains and nonlinear functional constrains for optimal design of high-power klystrons. This algorithm was implemented in the original code KlyOptim, that was tested on the problem of optimizing the parameters of a 50-megawatt S-band klystron built at the BINP SB RAS. To test the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, mass calculations of the parameters of a 6-resonator transient klystron were carried out with varying both the individual frequencies of the resonators and drift tubes, and their arbitrary combinations. As a result of the research, practical tolerances for the accuracy of manufacturing individual klystron units and the accuracy of tuning the electron beam bunching system were obtained. The optimization results are in good agreement with the data obtained by direct calculations with the klystron analysis code and with experimental data. A klystron of such power for powering the charged particle accelerators was first created in Russia and successfully passed the experimental tests.

articleTitle: Cognisant Simulation: New Age
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This article discusses new approaches and tools that help in the development and implementation of cognitive (intelligent) simulation models. The role of the agent-based approach to modeling is shown on the example of a real simulator for training drivers or pilots. It is shown that the main ideas of using artificial intelligence in simulation modeling are still relevant and can be used to build simulation models of large complex systems with structure and/or behavior uncertainty. Possible uncertainties in the description and behavior of the model are shown, as well as possible ways to resolve such situations using artificial intelligent (AI) tools and methods. The use of actors as the basis of intelligent simulation models is discussed. The vital role of storing the history of simulation models for learning actors is also discussed, as well as the problem of describing the behavior of actors representing people in simulation models.

articleTitle: TSP review: performance comparison of the well-known methods on a standardized dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Decades of research into the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) have yielded a plethora of algorithms, chiefly grouped into exact algorithms and heuristic/approximation algorithms. Exact algorithms, like the brute-force guarantee optimal solutions at the cost of exponential computational complexity. Conversely, heuristic algorithms, such as Greedy and natureinspired methods, offer sub-optimal solutions but with reduced computational demands. This study harnesses Reinelt Gerhard's TSPLIB dataset, featuring diverse TSP scenarios, including realworld challenges and problems crafted to gauge algorithmic efficacy in various contexts, like high-density clusters and Hamilton Cycle hard clusters. The research's crux is a comparative analysis of these TSP-solving techniques using TSPLIB. Subsequent sections delve into academic references, dataset methodologies, planned solutions, a juxtaposition of algorithmic results, culminating in concluding insights, that showed the shaked Nearest-Neighbor in current set of algorithms' implementation is the best, and it is worth trying to make it even better by applying some hybrid creative techniques, which is the subject of our future works.

articleTitle: Evaluating Large Language Models for Sentence Augmentation in Low-Resource Languages: A Case Study on Kazakh
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing (NLP) and demonstrated exceptional performance in various NLP tasks for widely spoken languages. However, their efficacy in handling low-resource languages remains an area of concern. This study investigates the performance of LLMs, particularly GPT-3, in sentence augmentation tasks for a low-resource language, Kazakh. We employ a blind peer review methodology, where five native Kazakh annotators assess the quality of LLM-generated augmentations. The results reveal that LLMs excel in popular languages like English, Chinese, and German, but face challenges with low-resource languages due to limited training data. This work sheds light on the importance of improving LLMs' adaptability and relevance to address the unique needs of low-resource languages. Further research could enhance the augmentation capabilities of LLMs in scenarios with limited data sources, ensuring their effectiveness in promoting linguistic diversity and inclusivity. Furthermore, this study underscores the significance of cross-language transfer learning and data collection efforts to empower LLMs in supporting linguistic diversity and fostering inclusivity across the global language landscape.

articleTitle: On Optimizing MEC Enabled Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In recent years, the use of sensor networks has grown very much, a large number of sensors are being introduced everywhere, which are used for various purposes - for example, monitoring the state of the air. In this article, we have described a proposal for IoT-based monitoring systems. Given the imperfection of the sensors, that is, the inaccuracy of measurements, it is necessary to optimize some parameters. The paper proposes a method for optimizing the threshold number of sensors that can detect an event of interest. This threshold-based detection scheme acts as a local decision-making mechanism and is used to implement the concept of multi-access computing. In turn, multi-access edge computing allows data from sensors to be processed close to users. This reduces system latency, provides faster analysis and immediate response to changing environmental conditions, reduces the amount of data transferred, and improves system security. We mainly consider air quality monitoring systems. However, the application range of the presented results is much wider.

articleTitle: The Comparative Analysis of Technologies and Software for Single Sign-On
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: The article provides the review and analysis of software products that implement support for single sign-on technology. Using single sign-on technology, users (in our case, employees of a research institute) move from one information system to another, unrelated to the first system, without re-authentication. The overview and brief description of the single sign-on systems types (enterprise and Web-based) is provided. The technological basis of such information systems is described (SAML language or OpenID standard). A number of currently existing software solutions are listed, grouped in terms of their licenses (proprietary international, proprietary local and free and open source international). The conclusion is drawn about feasibility of using single sign-on system with recommendations for the specific choice. Potential problems and disadvantages of such systems using are also mentioned. The review and analytical parts of the article are supported by links to actual publications on this topic.

articleTitle: Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Kazakh Text Generation Tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This paper presents an empirical study evaluating text generation models for the low-resource and morphologically complex Kazakh language. In this study, we leveraged a transformer-based neural architecture. Initially, we trained a large language model for the Kazakh language using a substantial text corpus. Then, we fine-tuned the base model using a specialized question-answering dataset. The proposed pretrained language model (PLM) was evaluated on a conversation response generation task, investigating its performance across domains and languages. The findings of cross-lingual comparison underlines the challenges of achieving good results for low-resource languages like Kazakh with current solutions. The experimental findings revealed that despite the low-resource characteristics of Kazakh language, Kazakh's PLMs and its fin-tuned model for question answering were obtained and its performance for the BLEU score was 8.5%, which was better than the random guess 4.01%. Additionally, Two Kazakh text corpora were collected for this work. One of datasets comprised a large collection of Kazakh text from different domains and was used to train a large language model. Second datasets were specifically collected for the question-answering task for Kazakh and Russian languages.

articleTitle: Decomposition Strategies for Solving a Large-Scale Consistent Vehicle Routing Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: A large-scale consistent vehicle routing problem is under consideration. In the problem, a company has a fleet of capacitated vehicles located in multiple depots, and there is a set of customers requiring a service. Vehicle routing is performed on a given planning horizon, and a vehicle should not exceed a limit on working hours per day. Each customer has a frequency of visits, which indicates how many times the customer must be visited during the planning horizon. Besides, to ensure consistency in the schedule, a customer should be visited by the same driver, and the time intervals between two consecutive visits must be the same. This allows the company to gain a competitive advantage by improving its service quality. Total travel costs are minimized in the problem while satisfying all the constraints. We present a POPMUSIC-based decomposition approach aimed to solve large-scale instances of the problem. The idea behind this approach is to improve the quality of a solution by iteratively solving subproblems of an overall problem. To get a solution for the overall problem and its subproblems, we use the variable neighborhood search (VNS) scheme developed by us previously. In the computational experiments section, we show a comparison of applying VNS for the whole problem and applying two different decomposition strategies: route- and customer-based ones.

articleTitle: A Heuristic Algorithm for the Temporal Knapsack Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We introduce a temporal knapsack problem originated in cloud computing. We have a server and a set of virtual machines (VMs). The server is divided by two identical NUMA nodes with their own CPU cores and RAM. For each VM, we know its CPU and RAM capacity, profit, and time interval when it is active. Some VMs we call small. We can put them in any NUMA node. Other VMs we call large. Such a VM occupies two nodes of the server and requires half of its own CPU and RAM on each node. We need to find a subset of VMs and their location on the server to maximize the total profit under the server's CPU and RAM capacity constraints during the whole-time interval. To tackle this NP-hard problem, we design an adaptive large neighborhood search method based on the destroy and repair approach. At the destroy stage, some VMs are removed from the current solution. At the repair stage, a new solution is created based on the tabu search meta-heuristic with flip and swap neighborhoods and penalties. To obtain an initial solution, we apply a fast greedy algorithm. Computational experiments are conducted for the semi-synthetic test instances with up to 500 VMs. Computational results are discussed and compared with the near-optimal solutions of commercial software Gurobi.

articleTitle: A Fitness Functions Based Algorithm for the Two-Dimensional Irregular Strip Packing Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We are given a finite set of items (irregular polygons) and a strip with known width and infinite length. The goal is to pack all items without overlapping so to minimize the used length of the strip. Rotation of items by discrete set of angles are allowed. We apply the well-known semi-discrete representation of the items in the strip. Each item and a strip are represents as a series of equidistant horizontal line segments. To receive the strip packing we apply the following iterative procedure. The number of iterations is equals to the number of items. The algorithm try to pack every unpacked item on every available place on the strip. For every item and for every place we calculate the fitness function. Our fitness function evaluate both the polygon to be packed and its packing place. At every iteration of the algorithm we evaluate unpacked polygons and a places to pack using the fitness functions. After that we construct the set of the combinations of the items and places with the biggest value of the fitness function. We randomly select one of this combinations to pack. This procedure is repeated while all objects is not packed. Because of the randomisation of this algorithm we need to repeat this algorithm for a several times to find a better result. Computational results for available test instances are discussed.

articleTitle: On the Core and Harsanyi Extensions of the Almost Positive Games
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In the paper, we study interconnections between the cores and other solutions of the Harsanyi extensions of almost positive cooperative games. A short and elementary proof is given establishing that the cores of Aubin extensions of the games mentioned above consist of their Shapley vectors. The proposed approach is based on a generalization of the classical notion of a balanced cover of the grand coalition to the case of fuzzy coalitions. This generalization allows us to expand the concept of a balanced ordinary cooperative game in situations where fuzzy blocking makes sense. In the preceding papers of the author it was shown that enlarging blocking capabilities by means of fuzzy coalitions doesn't prevent reasonable utilization of the linear programming methods (proved by O.N.Bondareva and L.S.Shapley to be very efficient in case of ordinary cooperative games). In particular, a criterion for the fuzzy game to have unblockable imputation turned out to be rather useful in clarifying some properties of Harsanyi extensions considered in the paper. One more example of the relevant application of the criterion mentioned is the main result of this work relating to the accessibility of core-imputations of the almost positive game via an appropriate fuzzy domination. Here we take into account, as well, a close correlation between the cores and superdifferentials of fuzzy cooperative games, mentioned by J.-P.Aubin.

articleTitle: Model for Long-Term Partnerships Between the Government and Subsoil Users in Production and Infrastructure Construction
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This paper explores a model of partnership between the state and private investors based on the clustering of fields and the creation of a system of consortia of private investors who jointly implement projects to build the necessary production infrastructure. This mechanism is based on a Stackelberg equilibrium search. The results of calculations based on real data of Zabaikalsky Krai allow us to formulate several practical recommendations on the formation of the equity construction mechanism and compensation policy. It is shown that the liberal investment policy of the state as a partner of the consortium system, to the greatest extent ensures the interests of both the budget and the private investor. The transition of the state to a conservative investment policy can be justified only in conditions of extremely tight budget constraints. The consequences of such a policy in Russian conditions lead to a reduction in the front of production and infrastructure construction and, as a consequence, discourage the entry of private investors into the underdeveloped raw material territory.

articleTitle: Using the Arc of a Great Circle to Search for the Best Metrological Characteristics of a Number of Projection Reference Systems when Cataloging Linear Engineering Objects
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Using BIM and GIS in cataloging systems of data on any location objects is an applied basis, behind which there are great possibilities of spatial data handling and obtaining new knowledge. The applied aspects of the present work particularize a range of opportunities to automate calculations by means of GIS in the formation of unique projection reference systems. Thus, for the ever it is suggested to use the parameter equation of the great circle arc as an engineered axis of projection. This approach allows for calculating the optimum position of the projection axis as a geodetic axis on the sphere using the least squares method, while ensuring the best metrological characteristics of the reference system. The specific features of representation of latitudes on the sphere and transition to spheroid surface and to the true values of deviations of cataloging object characteristic points through the spherical triangle solution are reviewed. The values that are the basis of text record of coordinate systems description in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${ }^*.\text{prj,}$</tex> PROJ.4, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*.\text{wkt}$</tex> formats are provided. The example of the calculated latitudes is provided for the projection axis when describing a linear object of the railroad, the values metrological having impact on distortions during transition to the plane are determined. The issues on transformation of the target function for solving the task on minimization of distortions and their limitations are proposed to be discussed.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Selecting Optimal Features in Face Recognition Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Biometric methods are divided into methods based on physical and habitual movements. Physical methods are based on the anatomical uniqueness of each person. Anatomical features include facial features, eye pupils, fingerprints, hand geometry, ear lobes, and other biometric features. Face recognition systems are based on anatomical features, the quality of which is related to the efficiency of feature extraction. Methods for generating face image features are usually based on the separation of local and global features. Algorithms for extracting local features extract individual parts of the face image and perform recognition based on them. Algorithms for extracting global features perform the formation of features on the entire face image. At the same time, the recognition of these features based on optimality allows to reduce costs. This article is devoted to the analysis of algorithms for the formation of the space of optimal features of a face image, which proposes the task of identifying optimal features, as well as a method and algorithm for extracting optimal features of a face image.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Hybrid Optimization Model of Personnel Digital Development Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: The object of our research is the organization personnel management department. The subject of our study is planning of the organization's employees digital competencies” development. The purpose of our work is to create a hybrid optimization model that allows for effective planning of the digital competencies development of the organization's personnel based on digital competencies assessments. The relevance of the research lies in the fact that with the active transition of world into the information environment all spheres. It is imperative that employees of organizations have the appropriate knowledge and skills. In our work, we considered and analyzed different approaches to effective planning for the personnel digital competencies” development, we developed and tested a hybrid optimization model that allows for planning the organization's employees digital competencies development based on assessments of digital competencies using machine learning and discrete optimization methods. The developed model has shown its effectiveness on test data. The use of the model will result in a more structured process of developing digital competencies of the organization's workers via a generated development schedule, as well as saving time an employee of the HR department would spend drawing up such a schedule.

articleTitle: Metaheuristics for Finding the Stability Radius in the Bilevel Facility Location and Uniform Pricing Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We consider a threshold stability problem for the facility location and uniform pricing problem with median-type location. In the threshold stability problem, the deviation from current customer budgets is maximized. The value of the maximum deviation is called threshold stability radius. The solution of the problem is called feasible if the leader's revenue is not less than a predetermined value (threshold) and it satisfies all the constraints of the facility location and uniform pricing problem for any deviation of budgets that does not exceed the threshold stability radius. In this paper, we develop two approximate algorithms for solving the threshold stability problem based on variable neighborhood descent (VND) heuristics. These algorithms are based on the ideas of finding optimal facility location or good approximate facility location and on the ideas of finding optimal pricing in the facility location and uniform pricing problem. The algorithms differ in the way of comparing different facility locations, which eventually leads to different estimates of the threshold stability radius. The numerical experiment has shown the efficiency of the chosen approach, both in terms of the running time of the algorithms and the quality of the obtained solutions.

articleTitle: Mean Field Optimal Control Problem for Predicting the Spread of Viral Infections
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: To describe the epidemic outbreak, we divide the entire population into five groups: susceptible to the virus (S), active infected (I), immune after vaccination or disease (R), vaccinated but not yet immune (V), and deceased (D), whose dynamics is described by SIR-type models and relies on the mass balance law. The population is considered rational and agents tend to choose isolation and vaccination strategies based on their own benefit, leading to an optimal control model. Such dynamic are described by mean field game (MFG) approach. A number of epidemiological scenarios have been constructed and computational results were compared with statistical data in Krasnoyarsk region for one month in 2022 to estimate the epidemiological situation in the region under consideration. MFG approach allows to take into account the heterogeneity of the population, which leads to the fact that the epidemiological MFG models are a kind of layer between simple differential SIR models and computationally complex agent based models.

articleTitle: Parallel Clustering Algorithm for the k-medoids Problem in High-dimensional Space for Large-scale Datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We present a robust, parallel primal-dual heuristic algorithm for the k-medoids clustering problem, a widely utilized method in data mining and machine learning. Our approach surpasses current algorithms by effectively addressing their limitations, such as time-consuming distance matrix calculations, inefficient nearest-neighbor searches, and difficulties in handling large-scale datasets. To overcome these challenges, we employ an efficient parallel implementation, combined with a pioneering subgradient search algorithm. We evaluate our algorithm on the BIRCH and Stanford Dog datasets and demonstrate its superiority over existing k-medoids clustering algorithms in terms of solution quality and run time. Additionally, we introduce a novel vectorization technique that enables our algorithm to handle various types of data, such as images, text, and point data. Overall, our work contributes to the field of data mining and machine learning by providing an efficient and effective solution for the k-medoids clustering problem. The proposed algorithm offers improved performance, and versatility, making it a valuable tool for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Tabu Search for the $(r\vert p)$-Centroid Problem Under Uncertainty*
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We consider the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r\vert p)$</tex>-centroid problem under an assumption of uncertainty in the input data. Two players, the leader and the follower, open facilities, striving to capture the largest market share. The leader opens p facilities, then the follower opens r facilities. Each customer chooses the nearest facility as his supplier and bring a particular income to the corresponding player. The aim is to choose p facilities of the leader in such a way as to maximize his market share. However, it is assumed that customers' purchasing power is not known exactly and can change after the decision made. This problem can be represented as a bilevel programming problem. In this work, we propose a local search approach based on a stochastic tabu search framework to tackle the problem. We provide the results of numerical experiments and compare the behavior of both players compared to the deterministic setting of the same problem.

articleTitle: A Grouping Genetic Algorithm for the Temporal Vector Bin Packing Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 19th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We consider the temporal vector bin packing problem, which has its origins in the field of cloud computing (Ratushnyi, Kochetov, 2021). Consider a finite collection of items, each associated with arrival and processing times, as well as two distinct weights or dimensions. A specific subset of items is designated as large items. Each bin possesses two capacities or dimensions, and it is partitioned into two identical sections. Large items are required to be split into two equal parts and allocated to both sections of a bin. Other items have the option to be placed in a single section of a bin, provided there is sufficient capacity in both dimensions. The objective is to efficiently fit all items into the least possible number of bins with matching dimensions. To address this challenge, we introduce a grouping genetic algorithm, compare its performance to the Column Generation heuristic, and outline the outcomes of a computational experiment. The evaluation of these algorithms was conducted using a publicly available dataset.
